title: Compiled assignment to a variable
statement: Let $Z$ be admissible compiler size data of word size $W$, with state $\sigma$ represented in a stack frame at depth $q$, where $1\le q$ and $q+F\le Q$. Suppose $x<F$, the code at $\mathrm{pos}$ begins with the two instructions that compute the address of local variable $x$ and store the value from address $c$ there, memory $m$ contains the word encoding $v$ at address $c$, and $c$ is not the address register. Then after two machine steps some memory $m'$ represents the state obtained from $\sigma$ by setting local variable $x$ to $v$, at the same stack depth $q$. The memories agree outside the writable-address set determined by $Z$ and $q$.
hypotheses_covered: Admissible size data Z and word size W
Initial memory represents σ in a framed stack at depth q
Code at pos begins with the specified address computation and store instructions
Memory at address c encodes v
c is distinct from the address register
